saints.name: St. Alphege of Canterbury
saints.title: Bishop and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: An archbishop who forbade his own ransom and was slain by Danish raiders…
biography: Born in 954, Alphege — Ælfheah in Old English — left his widowed mother for the monastery of Deerhurst and afterward lived as an anchorite at Bath, where he became abbot. In 984 he was made Bishop of Winchester, and in 994 he gave confirmation to Olaf of Norway at Andover.

Raised to Canterbury in 1006, he was taken prisoner in September 1011 when a Danish army sacked and burned the city. Held for months while a heavy ransom was demanded, he forbade his impoverished people to buy his life at their cost.

On 19 April 1012, at Greenwich, his captors, drunk with wine and enraged that the ransom was refused, pelted him with the bones of their feast and with stones, until one of them, named Thurm, dispatched him with an axe.

His body rested eleven years in St. Paul's, London, before King Canute translated it to Canterbury. Canonized in 1078, he found a defender of his martyrdom in Anselm of Canterbury, who taught that he who dies for truth and justice dies for Christ.
saints.knownFor: Refusing to let the poor be taxed for his ransom, and dying at Danish hands.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 19 April
